solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Poor actor allowed role beyond his capabilities

parts.note: a ham is an overacting, poor performer
let means permitted or allowed

explanation.surface: A bad actor is given a part far too demanding for him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: the great Shakespeare part is exactly the role a ham cannot manage.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is Shakespeare's most demanding lead part, notoriously beyond a mediocre performer.

clue.text: Missing persons in the family?

parts.note: read not as police cases but as people who miss their relatives and household

explanation.definitionFit: Someone longing for home and kin is missing the people at home, a cryptic twist on a police phrase.

clue.text: Chap getting work in France has to move smartly

parts.note: a chap is a man
oeuvre is the French word for a work

explanation.surface: A man who finds a job in France must relocate quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A manoeuvre is a skilful, deft movement, so the verb means to move cleverly into position.

clue.text: It's not difficult to name a novel midshipman

definitions.meaning: Mr Midshipman ... is the title hero of Captain Marryat's 1836 naval novel

explanation.surface: Naming a fictional junior naval officer is a simple task.
explanation.walkthrough: Marryat's novel follows young Jack Easy at sea in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple and effortless tasks are the opposite of hard; the second sense is a fictional sailor's surname.

clue.text: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch

definitions.text: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch

parts.words: In which all entrants won't come up to scratch
parts.note: in a race where runners start at staggered marks, only the best begins at the scratch line

explanation.walkthrough: 'Come up to scratch' seems to mean 'be good enough', but scratch is the starting mark of the strongest runner in a race with staggered starts.
explanation.definitionFit: In such a race weaker entrants get a head start, so not everyone begins from the scratch mark.

clue.text: Shocking in respect to certain individuals

parts.note: awe is deep, reverent respect
some means certain people, an unspecified few

explanation.surface: Something is scandalous as regards particular people.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something staggering enough to stun or overwhelm, a near synonym in current use.

clue.text: One who follows another about in training

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the follower's word goes round the next one

parts.note: a disciple is a follower of a teacher
taken as written

explanation.surface: A follower trails someone round during instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Training in obedience and self-control is a synonym, as in military drill.

clue.text: Grain leaving a tropic island

indicators.note: the grain word departs from the tropic's name, removing those letters

parts.note: the Tropic of Capricorn is the southern tropic line of latitude
corn is cereal grain

explanation.surface: Grain is shipped out of a tropical island.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian isle in the Bay of Naples is a famous holiday resort.

clue.text: Tear after father — or mother

indicators.note: after puts the tear word behind the father word

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a rent is a rip or tear in fabric

explanation.surface: A rip appears after Dad, or perhaps Mum.
explanation.definitionFit: A mother is one example of a person who has borne or raised a child.

clue.text: Bound to be working to scold someone vigorously

parts.note: to bound is to leap or jump
on means operating, switched on

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to be busy telling people off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be', but Bound is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To pounce on someone verbally is to rebuke them sharply, an informal idiom.

clue.text: Without a clue perhaps? That's fine

parts.note: minus means lacking or without

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the clue word's letters may be rearranged in another order

explanation.surface: A solver lacking any hint is told that is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'clue'. 'That's fine' looks like approval, but fine here means very small, as in fine print.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine in the sense of very thin or tiny matches this word for extremely small.

clue.text: Police officer's half-hearted meal

indicators.note: one of the meal's two central letters, half its heart, is lost

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A constable eats a meagre dinner without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two Ps at the centre of SUPPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal short form of superintendent, a senior rank in British police forces.

clue.text: Outhouse made redundant

explanation.definitionFit: A garden hut is a small outbuilding; firms lose surplus staff, cutting jobs.

clue.text: Not the government's workplace

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
position means a place or location

explanation.surface: A rival party's office is somewhere other than government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workplace' splits into two pieces, work (OP, from opus) and place.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliament the parties not in power form the rival bench facing ministers.

clue.text: Essential mood

definitions.meaning: the grammatical mood used for commands

explanation.definitionFit: Something vital is a must; in grammar the command form of a verb is a mood.

clue.text: Club retainer who used to drag his wife along

definitions.text: Club retainer who used to drag his wife along

parts.words: Club retainer who used to drag his wife along
parts.note: not a club servant but a prehistoric man holding a club, from the cartoon image of dragging a mate by the hair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Club retainer' suggests a club's staff member, but it is someone who retains, holds, a club.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon Stone Age man carries a club and drags his partner off by her hair.

clue.text: Enrol recruit

definitions.meaning: take on as a member, especially for the armed forces

explanation.definitionFit: To sign up for service, or to take someone on, both senses of joining forces.

clue.text: Pleased to have met

definitions.meaning: fulfilled, as requirements or conditions are met

explanation.definitionFit: Content and fulfilled are both senses: a happy person, or a condition fulfilled.

clue.text: Sounds like a habit to get used to

indicators.note: says the words for a habit are spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: a custom is a habit or practice

explanation.surface: A routine seems like something you adapt to.
explanation.definitionFit: To accustom oneself is to become familiar or habituated with something.

clue.text: Parts always carried by a seagoing vessel

indicators.note: the vessel carries the always word aboard, around it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ever means always

explanation.surface: Ship parts are permanently aboard an ocean vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parts' looks like a noun but is the verb: cuts apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To part is to divide or cut off, as a rope is cut through.

clue.text: Schoolchild's book case

parts.note: not a shelf unit but a case in which books are carried to school

explanation.definitionFit: A pupil's shoulder bag carries books and homework to school.

clue.text: In fact a wild enthusiast

indicators.note: wild means out of order, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: Indeed a frantic devotee.
explanation.definitionFit: A zealot or obsessive devotee is an extreme enthusiast.

clue.text: Lord, if drunk, becomes flushed

indicators.note: a drunk person's words come out jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A peer who drinks goes red in the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A florid complexion is ruddy and red, as of a flushed face.

clue.text: Loves someone so dear, madly

indicators.note: madly means wildly, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone is loved intensely, being so precious.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship or deeply cherish a person is to love them.

clue.text: Not a direct form of slander

indicators.note: a different form of the words means their letters reshaped

explanation.surface: Defamation is an indirect kind of attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Detraction is disparagement of someone's reputation, a synonym of slander.

clue.text: High place for a bird to live in

indicators.note: the live word goes inside the bird's name

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A lofty spot is good for a bird to inhabit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan plateau region is known as the roof of the world, a lofty location.

clue.text: He sold his birthright in the sausage factory

indicators.note: says the answer is tucked inside the following words

explanation.surface: Someone traded his inheritance at a meat processing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis Esau sells his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of stew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament figure traded his birthright to Jacob for a meal of pottage.

clue.text: Is half left in the water

indicators.note: half asks for the first two of the four letters of left

explanation.surface: Half the remains lie in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: an island is land in the water.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land surrounded by sea, so it sits in the water.

clue.text: Teacher to talk for ages, short of time

indicators.note: short of means lacking, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: to rabbit on is British slang for chattering endlessly

explanation.surface: An instructor goes on and on, running late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' (on) is British slang for talking at length.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious leader and scholar; the word itself means my master or teacher.

clue.text: An annoying habit of the conscience-stricken

definitions.text: An annoying habit of the conscience-stricken

parts.words: An annoying habit of the conscience-stricken
parts.note: habit as garment: a scratchy shirt worn as penance by the guilty

explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' means clothing, not behaviour, and 'annoying' means literally irritating to the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse goat-hair garment worn as penance by the pious or guilty.

clue.text: Fixed menus that could be meatless

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Set lunch options might be vegetarian.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixed-price menus of preset courses are called table d'hote.

clue.text: When models that have lost their shape are employed?

definitions.text: When models that have lost their shape are employed?

indicators.note: the word models is bent out of shape, its letters reordered

explanation.surface: When do out-of-shape models get work?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue answers itself: out-of-shape models get work rarely.
explanation.definitionFit: Models past their best are rarely hired, so the answer means infrequently.
